candidates.change: `granule_size: 16 -> 8` — ZBU detector split into 2 per-row granules (2 x 64b OR-reduce, 2 bitmap bits/row, row skip = AND)
candidates.rationale: A is unstructured at exactly 6.25% density (macs_useful/macs_issued); granule 16 captures 0.9375^16 = 35.6% of A elements in all-zero granules, granule 8 captures 59.6% — the T-B SRAM credit is derived from the all-zero granule population, and 16 is the *coarsest* legal value, not a tuned one

the SpMM schedule never issues LAYERNORM/IGELU/SOFTMAX or CONFIG_NORM, so the Normalizer (2 stats, 16 int32 reduce lanes) and the three activation branches in AccumulatorScale are synthesised, leaked and charged to `area_um2` while holding nothing — `is_passthru = !has_normalizations` deletes the whole block; it is the "remove capacity the software schedule no longer needs" half of the diagnosis applied to a functional unit rather than an SRAM

`dma_maxbytes = 64` = 4 DIM-column tiles, so b_blocks=4 exactly fills one DMA request and cuts the X mvin instruction count 4x; never swept, and a software-only move costs a third of the wall clock — but `dma_wait_fraction = 0.01` says the load path is not stalling, so the expected cycle gain is small
